slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Many proofs combine parallel lines with congruent triangles. Parallel lines give equal alternate interior or corresponding angles; those angles feed ASA or AAS; CPCTC then gives the equal parts.

Example: in quadrilateral ABCD, AB is parallel to CD and AB = CD. Draw diagonal AC. Angle BAC = angle DCA (alternate interior angles), AB = CD and AC = CA, so triangle ABC is congruent to triangle CDA by SAS. Then BC = DA by CPCTC.

slides.html: In the example, which pair of parallel lines gave the equal angles, and which line was the transversal?
slides.reveal: AB and CD were the parallels, and diagonal AC was the transversal.
